main_text.p: fua manu in libertate vindicent, ne etiā excusso Tyranni iugo sibi Regem eligat, qui legibus subiiciatur exemplo Polonorum ducti, tum temporis precibus vix locus superesset: memineris quid de occasione dictum sit olim:
Fronte capillata post terga occasio calua est.
Postremò (mi honorāde domine) Deum precor tibi addat animos, vt me impulsore, tuae patriae vicem misertus regnum capessere velis à Tyranno, mulierculis, Italis, ganeonibus & lenonibus dilapidatū.
Vt tuis etiam incœptis faueat, teq; & tuos nobis seruet incolumes.

page.notes: Printed text is in a larger-set roman; "impulsore" and "patriae" are as printed in the scan's line breaks ("impulso-re"). Dating line "1574" is set with a superior style, shown as printed. The line "Fronte capillata..." is a verse line set as its own paragraph; the pentameter "ua est." is its continuation. Faint show-through text on the right side of the scan is not transcribed.
